meaning_fix: thing / matter; a job or task to do
reasoning: Taa marbuta after ل is e. شغلة is the general Palestinian 'thing / matter' (شغلة بسيطة); it does not specifically mean a household chore.
A written-Arabic phrase, as the English itself flags; in Ramallah conversation people simply say masalan. م is a moon letter, so il-mithaal.
Long ee, not ii: beet, distinct from biit. Written with kasra plus ya, the Palestinian way of spelling this vowel.
Dual of marra with the short vowel syncopated, so the doubled r meets the t directly. The dual ending is long ee.
The tanween of أهلاً is actually pronounced, so it is written and romanized -an. Word-initial hamza is not romanized.
Palestinian geminates the ف and has kasra in the first syllable, shiffe, unlike MSA shafa. Taa marbuta after ف is e.
ابن is said with an epenthetic vowel, ibin, when nothing precedes it. خالة is the mother's sister, so the English gloss is exact.
Urban Palestinian merges ظ into ض, so الظهر is said and often written الضهر, with the sun-letter assimilation iD-Duhur and an echo vowel in the final cluster.

meaning_fix: field / arena; a town square is ساحة or دوّار
reasoning: Long ee then long aa. In Ramallah ميدان is mostly figurative ('in the field'); a public square is a saa7a, and a roundabout square is a dawwaar.
ذ is realised z in this learned word, so it is respelled, and the final cluster takes an echo vowel: 3uzur. Also heard as the phrase عندو عذر.
Form II passive participle with the Palestinian m- cluster and shadda on the م; ص is emphatic S.
ق is a glottal stop in this everyday word; the ن is assimilated towards m before the ب in fast speech. Taa marbuta after ل is e.
bi plus 'addeesh asks a price. The hamza of الإيجار is written because it follows the article prefix, and ش is a sun letter: bish-shahar.
The -an tanween adverb is a written-Arabic pattern; Ramallah speakers say bin-naadir or قليل ما بصير. Educated speakers do use naadiran in semi-formal talk.
ناحية loses its medial vowel: naa7ye. ثانية is taanye in Palestinian, so it is respelled with ت; both end in taa marbuta e.
ض is emphatic D with long aa. تلفون, not هاتف, is the Palestinian word, with long oo.
keef with long ee, not MSA kayfa. The hamza is written after the article prefix: il-'awlaad.
ط is emphatic T; the medial vowel drops and the taa marbuta after ل is e.
Long aa in zamaan. It covers both 'a long time ago' and 'for a long time now', as in min zamaan ma shuftak.
kull-ma sets up 'the more / whenever'. The first person past of كبر drops its first vowel: kbirt.
The noun takes an echo vowel in the final cluster: ribi7. Spelled identically to the verb ribi7 'he won'.
Optative with no b- prefix. أيام has a doubled y and the possessive -o, a stock nostalgic phrase.
كنيسة loses its first vowel and takes -et in the construct, respelled with ت. ق glottalises even in this name as locals say it; the hamza is written after the article.
The first short vowel reduces to a cluster in Palestinian speech, with long ii in the stressed syllable.
ليلة has long ee and takes -et in the construct. imbaari7 is the Palestinian 'yesterday', with its initial vowel written as part of the seat.
